known_facts_book1: Is the flower Alice addresses first, wishing it could talk, and answers 'We can talk, when there's anybody worth talking to.'
Says the flowers can talk as well as Alice can, and a great deal louder.
Remarks that Alice would be all right if only her petals curled up a little more.
Silences the daisies by waving itself passionately from side to side, and says they are worst of all.
Explains that the flowers here can talk because the beds are hard, whereas in most gardens the beds are made too soft and the flowers are always asleep.
Tells the Violet to hold its tongue, since it keeps its head under the leaves and snores.
Says of the Red Queen that her petals are done up close, almost like a dahlia.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Criticises her shape and colour, then explains why the flowers of this garden are awake.
known_relations_book1.Rose: The other talking flower of the bed, who speaks with it about Alice and the Red Queen.
known_relations_book1.Daisy: The chorus of daisies it silences with a threat they cannot answer.

known_facts_book1: Says it isn't manners for the flowers to begin, and that it was wondering when Alice would speak.
Judges that Alice's face has got some sense in it though it's not a clever one, and that she is the right colour.
Says the tree in the middle of the bed is good for nothing but saying 'Bough-wough'.
Tells Alice she never thinks at all, and that she is beginning to fade, so her petals get untidy.
Describes the Red Queen as another flower that can move about, redder and bushier than Alice, and one of the thorny kind who wears her thorns round her head.
Advises Alice to walk the other way in order to meet the Red Queen, which turns out to be the only thing that works.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Insults and advises her in the same breath; its advice about walking backwards is what gets her to the Red Queen.
known_relations_book1.Tiger-lily: The flower it converses with over Alice's head.
known_relations_book1.Red Queen: Described to Alice as the other flower in the garden that can move about.

known_facts_book1: Forms the border of the flower-bed, and one of them cries that the tree says 'Bough-wough!' — that's why its branches are called boughs.
The daisies all begin shouting together till the air seems full of little shrill voices.
Fall silent in a moment when Alice stoops down and whispers that she will pick them, and several of the pink ones turn white.
Are called the worst of all by the Tiger-lily, because when one speaks they all begin together.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Silenced by her threat to pick them.
known_relations_book1.Tiger-lily: The flower that keeps ordering them to be quiet.

not_in_this_book: the daisies are picked by Alice
